> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6673c8018f1223bd2f7a8eb2fde1123b756819f4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d93fae67a268abaadfab6b1e885beacc1f9c6204` — the merge of head `592e1bd8a98dd72e8f84c61d1bf2f0f3b2a43d7c` into base `6673c8018f1223bd2f7a8eb2fde1123b756819f4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d93fae67a268abaadfab6b1e885beacc1f9c6204 && git checkout d93fae67a268abaadfab6b1e885beacc1f9c6204
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6673c8018f1223bd2f7a8eb2fde1123b756819f4 592e1bd8a98dd72e8f84c61d1bf2f0f3b2a43d7c && git checkout -B drift-repro 6673c8018f1223bd2f7a8eb2fde1123b756819f4 && git merge --no-ff 592e1bd8a98dd72e8f84c61d1bf2f0f3b2a43d7c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6673c8018f1223bd2f7a8eb2fde1123b756819f4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6673c8018f1223bd2f7a8eb2fde1123b756819f4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `592e1bd8a98dd72e8f84c61d1bf2f0f3b2a43d7c`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23168 (body and all twelve comments, among them triage's contract choice `6139317450`, the first round's report `6148078184`, the fork answer `6148462268`, the landing record `6149320013`, the claim `6151841916`, the report `6154277169` and the ACCEPT `6154370990`), PR #23331's body, comments and file list, the net diff `origin/main...592e1bd8a` (merge base `404fc477e`; 9 files, +482 / −56), the ruled half `b529a5c23` (PR #23289), objectui's runner at the `.objectui-sha` pin `1fb1ced36243` and at objectui `main` `72594f29` (`git show` only), `origin/main` for context, and the head's check-runs. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The refused set is triage's C exactly — right.** `rowOnSuccessRefused(executor)` is `executor === undefined || (ROW_BUILTIN_EXECUTORS.has(executor) && !ON_SUCCESS_EXECUTORS.has(executor))`, with `ROW_BUILTIN_EXECUTORS = ActionType.options ∪ ROW_URL_NAVIGATOR_EXECUTORS` = `script, url, modal, flow, api, form, navigation` and `ON_SUCCESS_EXECUTORS = api, script`. So `onSuccess` is refused beside `url`, `navigation`, `modal`, `flow`, `form` and beside no effective executor; `api`, `script` and every other name (a host handler: `run`, `clone_task`) stay open. The seven are read from the contract's own vocabulary, not re-spelled, and they equal the runner's `builtinExecutors` table at the pin (`packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts:1140-1152`, a `Record` keyed by `RunnableActionType`), which I confirmed byte-identical at objectui `main` `72594f29` (`git diff --stat` between the two is empty).
2. **One resolution, the runner's — right.** The rule reads `effectiveRowExecutor(row, executorKey)` = `row[executorKey] || row.name || undefined` (landed by `b529a5c23`), the runner's `action.type || action.actionType || action.name || ''` (`:1265`). A declared key outranks `name` (`actionType: 'api'` with `name: 'url'` parses; `actionType: 'form'` with `name: 'api'` is refused), an empty key falls through to `name`, and `name: ''` with no key resolves to no executor. All pinned in section 3 of `component-action-row-on-success-executor.test.ts`, each with a negative control.
3. **The four rows are judged identically — right.** `refuseRowOnSuccessBesideExecutor` is a sibling factory chained after the url-target and alias refinements on `ActionButtonPropsSchema`, `ActionIconPropsSchema`, the `action:group` member and the `action:menu` member; the issue lands at `onSuccess` with code `custom`. The props gate reports it at `properties.onSuccess` / `properties.actions.0.onSuccess` (the lint pins' `BASE` and `BASE.actions.0`), and `packages/lint/src` is untouched: only its test file changes. A `navigation` row gets two issues in chain order (alias at the key, then `onSuccess`), pinned.
4. **The shared refusal text is true for each executor, read at the pin — right.** `url` / `navigation`: `executeUrl` and `executeNavigation` hand to `navigateTo`, then every branch of `execute` ends in `handlePostExecution`, which hops on `result.success && action.onSuccess` (`:1639-1642`); a second navigation. `form`: `executeForm` answers `{ success: true, redirect: '/forms/NAME' }` and the hop follows. `modal`: the console registers `modal: modalActionHandler` (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:803`), and `useActionModal` resolves when the dialog closes — a saved form `{ success: true, reload: true, data }`, OK `{ success: true }`, a dismissal `{ success: false }`; with no host the runner answers `{ success: true, modal }` at once. So "whatever the dialog's host answers", not "a second hop": the dev's correction of the dispatch text is right. `flow`: the console registers `flow: flowHandler`, which judges through `judgeFlowLaunch` (`app-shell/src/utils/flowResponse.ts`): `paused` and `refused` both answer `{ success: true, silent: true }`, so the hop fires with the screen or the refusal notice open. No executor: `''` matches no handler and no built-in, so the row lands in `executeActionSchema` and no hop runs. One module, `action-on-success-executor.ts`, prints the text for the action and the rows, and the ONE TEXT pin holds the row's message after its subject byte-equal to `ActionSchema`'s.
5. **`ActionSchema`'s reach is unchanged — right.** The `.refine` became a `.superRefine` at the same point in the chain, same path `['onSuccess']`, same code `custom`, predicate `!ON_SUCCESS_EXECUTORS.has(data.type)` over the closed `ActionType` enum with its `script` default, so `url`, `modal`, `flow`, `form` are refused as before and `api`, `script` accepted (new negative controls). Only the reason changed, and the old one was false: the runner hops after every executor, so "no renderer reads a post-success hop today" was not true at the pin.
6. **Nothing published is widened — right.** The new module is reached by relative import from `action.zod.ts` and `component.zod.ts` only; it is not in the `ui` barrel (`index.ts` exports `action.zod` and `component.zod`, nothing else of this family) and neither file re-exports it — the same shape as `action-target-aliases.ts` and `navigation-target.ts`, for the reason that file states. `component.zod.ts` newly imports `ActionType` from `action.zod.ts`, which does not import back, so no cycle under the module-level `ROW_BUILTIN_EXECUTORS`. The `api-surface`, `export-origins` and `authorable-surface` baselines are not in the diff, and the lint-family check-runs that run those gates (`check:export-origins`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:api-surface`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:spec-changes` in `lint.yml`) are `success` on this head.
7. **The describes and the regenerated reference — right.** "no `actionType`" became "no or an empty `actionType`" (`type` on a member) on the `name` and `target` describes; the three `onSuccess` describes state the executor scope; `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx` is the regenerated output and nothing else in it moved.
8. **The D3 entry and FROM → TO — right.** `18.ui-page-action-row-on-success-beside-executor-refused.ts` names the surface (all four rows, key or name leg, no or empty executor), the replacement per executor, a reason that matches the measured runtime, and a mechanical acceptance criterion; step 18 is the step of every sibling entry and of the ruled half's; `os migrate meta --from 17` lists it, as the changeset says. The changeset's FROM → TO table carries one row per refused arm (`url`, `navigation`, `form`, `modal` / `flow`, no executor) with the one-line fix. One nit, not a flag: the entry's `surface` holds backticks, which `scripts/build-upgrade-guide.ts:135` wraps in a code span of its own; the landed sibling `18.ui-page-action-row-name-leg-url-target-judged.ts` does the same and passed `check:upgrade-guide`, so this is the family's existing pattern, for whoever next touches the generator.
9. **Producers.** My own scan of the head (`examples`, `packages/qa`, `packages/cli/src`, `content/docs`, `skills`, `packages/platform-objects`, tests excluded) finds no page action row carrying `onSuccess` beside a refused executor; the hits are `ActionSchema`'s reference tables and generated translation keys. The one objectui site is the one the dev named (item ③).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23168-page-action-row-on-success-beside-executor.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, headed `feat(spec)!:`, `**BREAKING**`, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and exactly one adr-0087 marker (`registered ui-page-action-row-on-success-beside-executor-refused`), the FROM → TO table and the one-line fix. Right on every count:

- **The arm.** Nothing is newly accepted; the rows' accept-set shrinks on one key. `no (narrowing)` is the declaration AGENTS.md names for that, it is BREAKING, and the changeset says so and carries its migration. The PR body's line 2 reads the same.
- **The level.** `minor` for an accept-set narrowing is the launch-window convention the ruled half of this same card shipped under (`b529a5c23`, PASS on its own contract review) and every other BREAKING `@objectstack/spec` changeset on `origin/main` carries (`23015`, `23082`, `23100`, `23103`, `23168` name-leg, `23228`).
- **The packages.** The diff publishes into `@objectstack/spec` alone. `packages/lint` changes only a test file (nothing published), and `content/docs` is the site. One changeset is the right count, and `skip-changeset` does not apply.

### ③ Boundary flags

Report `6154277169`, every deviation and every out-of-scope entry:

- **Commit trailers in AGENTS.md's model-free pair** (`Claude-Session` + `Co-authored-by: Claude`), not the harness reminder's model-named form — answered: AGENTS.md outranks the reminder by its own header and the pre-push hook refuses a model identifier; the three authored commits carry the pair, the merge commit carries git's default body.
- **Scratchpad reuse of `issue-23168/`** — answered: process only; the previous round is closed and nothing in the diff depends on it.
- **A `bash -c` gate loop blocked by the harness; the six reruns from a script file** — answered: nothing ran in the blocked form, and the six exit 0 on the rerun at the same head.
- **Two lock-budget waits on the workspace build** — answered: process only.
- **`check:type-check-debt` NOT MEASURED (killed by the dev's own timeout)** — answered by CI: `Type Check · debt ledger` is `completed / success` on this head.
- **Out-of-scope 1, `operation: 'update'` rows (carrier: none)** — answered on the verdict, escalated on the carrier. Under C as ruled, a row with no executor key and no `name` has no effective executor (`key || name`), and such a row is refused; the runner's `operation`-first dispatch (`:1384-1388`) does not change what the contract's effective executor is. The verdict is also the one `ActionSchema` already gives: it refuses `onSuccess` beside `operation: 'update'` on every `type` (`action.zod.ts`, the "`onSuccess` is not defined for an `operation: 'update'` action yet" refinement on `origin/main`). So it is not a defect in this PR: nothing is newly accepted, and the refusal is right. What is imprecise for that one shape is the text — "has no executor to follow" and the `actionType: 'script'` prescription are inert there, since the runner reads `operation` first and hops after the write — and no producer carries it. The gap underneath predates this PR and is outside the card: the rows' `operation` is `z.unknown()`, so the rows never carried `ActionSchema`'s `operation: 'update'` + `onSuccess` rule, and `{ operation: 'update', actionType: 'script', onSuccess }` parses on a row while `ActionSchema` refuses the same shape. That is a contract divergence with a static repro, and "carrier: none" is not a carrier under Prime Directive #10. ESCALATED to the owning seat: file the card for the rows' `operation: 'update'` posture (dedupe words: page action row operation update onSuccess; rows operation z.unknown; declarative update row hop). No change to this PR.
- **Out-of-scope 2, the rows-wide "VALUE posture" docblock** — answered: confirmed stale at the head (`component.zod.ts:3947` still lists `onSuccess` among the `z.unknown()` keys); a comment, not a contract; the named carrier (the next PR to touch that docblock) is acceptable.
- **The objectui red site** — answered: `packages/types/src/__tests__/held-public-block-arms-10872.test.ts:224` at objectui `main` `72594f29` asserts an executor-less, nameless row with `onSuccess` accepted on both faces, as the dev and triage read it; the seat filed objectstack-ai/objectui#12338 (open, `pm:on-hold`, with its Restart-when line), as fork answer `6148462268` asked. The `Console Pin Gate` is `skipped` on this head, so nothing reds in this repo.
- **The pin citations** — answered: the PR body and the new docblocks cite `core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` lines `1140-1152`, `1265`, `1384-1388`, `1639-1642`; each resolves to what it claims at `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` at the pin (the repo's existing citation spelling, as `effectiveRowExecutor`'s docblock on `main` uses it).
- **Check-runs on this head at the last read before this post:** 40 runs; 35 `completed`, every one `success` or `skipped` on the expected roster (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, the Dogfood matrix template, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke), none red; **5 still `in_progress`: `Test Core (2/6)` through `(6/6)`** (`Test Core (1/6)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Type Check · debt ledger` completed `success`). Reported as such, not assumed. The landing waits on them by the seat's own pre-queue rule; this record judges the contract change.
